name_note: Older papers call this species Lactobacillus ruminis; the name Ligilactobacillus ruminis follows the 2020 reclassification of the genus Lactobacillus.

sentences.text: Ligilactobacillus ruminis is a flagellated lactic acid bacterium found in the intestines of various mammals, including humans.
It has been described as an autochthonous gut commensal that relies on sortase-dependent LrpCBA pili for host adherence and persistence.
A genome report described a strain of this species isolated from the human colon as a prospective probiotic candidate.

Among Lactobacillus strains cultured from faecal samples of healthy young people in Tibet, Xinjiang and Inner Mongolia, Lactobacillus ruminis was a dominant species, making up 54.4 percent of isolates.
